records.title: Attribute a red guard to the change that broke it and say how to fix it
records.summary: Fast guards no longer block merges, so a red guard on main needs an owner fast. ci-guard-attribution.yml runs after every CI fast guards or repository-variables run: it walks back to the last green run, re-runs only the failing step on each first-parent commit in between, names the culprit PR with the exact assertion, the likely fix and a one-line repro, keeps one tracking issue per red workflow, and offers mechanical fix patches.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 14768
evidence.basis: PR body: a hand-run replay, 'analyze --sha 90e8953 --log <fast guards at 90e8953> --baseline 90e8953~4', ran the failing step on 4 commits, found 90e8953 (#14724) first to fail, and took 92 s and 2 API calls. It was given the log and a hand-set 4-commit baseline, so the 92 s excludes the workflow_run trigger, runner start and log fetch, and ranges over 40 commits are bisected by halving. At 90e8953 the fix was a hint, not a verified patch. The dry-run report it would have posted, naming #14724 and the missing CI_SEED_KEEP_LOCAL_RUNNERS exemption, is in the PR's replay comment (issuecomment-5841155073). No numeric claim is made: there is no measured before time, and no live attribution has happened yet (no CI fast guards run on main failed in the controller's webhook feed from 00:42 to 04:42Z 09-26).

records.title: PR picker fills idle and briefly busy owned minis before Blacksmith
records.summary: The PR runner picker capped the owned pool's allowance at Blacksmith's expected wait from a snapshot up to 45 min old, charged owned labels for in-flight peaks of jobs that did not exist yet, and fell back to the default Blacksmith route when the snapshot download failed. It now reads live runners, takes a run onto the owned pool while its jobs start within the configured queue rounds, and treats Blacksmith as overflow. In the first, lightly loaded night hours after merge, PR CI's attempt-1 macOS 26 work moved from a swinging 39% to 85% (56% overall) to about 89% on the owned minis, and its queue wait fell. Blacksmith re-runs of refused jobs rose over the same hours, so this is not a fleet-wide Blacksmith saving.

evidence.basis: Measured after merge from the build controller's workflow_job webhook feed (no API calls), read 04:42Z 09-26. Attempt 1 of in-repository pull_request CI runs, macOS 26 jobs that ran (glaeda-* or *-macos-26 labels), run windowed by its first job's creation. Before (runs 00:45 to 02:17Z): 144 runs, 54 with any Blacksmith macOS 26 job; 1,206 owned and 942 Blacksmith job-minutes (56.2% owned); 6.5 Blacksmith min per run; queue wait p50 200 s, p90 2,565 s. After (runs 02:17 to 04:00Z): 60 runs, 2 with any Blacksmith job; 613 owned and 77 Blacksmith job-minutes (88.9% owned); 1.3 Blacksmith min per run; queue wait p50 17 s, p90 340 s. Owned runners busy 23.4 of 37.9 online before and 21.2 of 39.2 after (ci-dash utilization).

records.title: UI E2E runs adopt the app and UI test bundle PR CI compiled
records.summary: UI E2E dispatches from scripts/run-e2e.sh used to compile the whole app again even though the PR's own CI compile admission already builds the cmuxUITests bundle. The dispatcher now finds the in-repository PR CI run for the commit, keeps the head when the merge has the same product inputs, waits for an in-flight admission, and test-e2e.yml adopts that product, so the build job skips its compile step.

evidence.label: CMUX PR 14776
evidence.basis: PR body 'Timing against the old full build' and 'UI E2E volume', rechecked from the two runs' build-job step times. Old full build: run 36197213485 (22:32Z 09-25, build job 108275782583 on glaeda-root-std-xcode-26.6): run created 22:32:38, build job start 22:34:11, compile step 'Build the app-host and UI test product' 22:35:44 to 22:43:12 (7 min 28 s), tests start 22:43:37 (step 37 'Run the selected tests here', which ran the tests on this side), so 659 s from run creation and 566 s from build-job start to tests; last update 22:49:00. Adopted product: run 36216682336 (04:03Z 09-26, build job 108333960534 on blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-26): run created 04:03:23, build job created 04:03:45 and started 04:05:44 (119 s Blacksmith queue), compile step skipped, 'Reuse a compiled product' 43 s, tests start 04:07:33 (step 39 'Run selected tests'; 'Run the selected tests here' took 0 s on this side), so 250 s from run creation and 109 s from build-job start; last update 04:09:04. The selector RemoteTmuxSizingUITests/testAttachSettlesStableAndCoherent is in both runs' names. Both runs ended red for reasons outside the build step: the old run's 'Run selected tests' wrapper failed 3 s after its tests ran, and the new run hit an app-activation guard on that Blacksmith runner (PR body). Volume baseline from the PR body: 12.3 h of test-e2e.yml history, 400 runs, 269 UI runs; 117 of 180 UI build jobs compiled, median compile step 413 s, 917 compile-minutes in total.

claims.metric: UI E2E run creation to test start, one selector, product already published at dispatch
claims.population: One full-build UI E2E run on an owned mini (glaeda-root-std-xcode-26.6) against one adopted-product run on blacksmith-12vcpu-macos-26
claims.note: 659 s to 250 s from run creation to test start; the build-job window alone went 566 s to 109 s (457 s), but time before the build job grew from 93 s to 141 s (a 119 s Blacksmith queue), so the run-level figure is claimed. This is the best case: the adopted run found a finished product. When the dispatch starts while admission is still compiling, the dispatcher now waits for it (up to 50 min), and the saving is the compile step minus that remaining wait, which can be negative: #14746's own head (this before run, created 22:32:38) had an admission that published at about 22:41, so waiting for it and then adopting (93 to 141 s before the build job plus about 109 s to tests) would have started its tests at about 22:44 to 22:45, roughly 0.5 to 1.5 min later than the 22:43:37 they did. Run creation to test start never includes the dispatcher's wait, because the dispatcher waits before it creates the run. One run each side, on different pools: the old run compiled on an owned mini, the new one adopted a Blacksmith-compiled product on Blacksmith, because products never cross toolchain families. The removed work is the 448 s compile step, so the pool difference matters less than it would for a compile comparison, but it is not like-for-like. Whole run (created to last update, not the PR table's 976 s job-span figure) went from 982 s to 341 s; about 193 s of the old figure is a late product upload after the tests that the adopted run skips, so the whole-run delta is not claimed separately. Only UI runs whose commit has an in-repository PR CI product on macOS 26 benefit. The PR merged at 04:33:43Z and had no adopted production runs yet at recording time, so this stays observed until a median over post-merge UI runs exists.

claims.metric: UI E2E build jobs that compiled the app
claims.measurementWindow: 12.3 h of test-e2e.yml history before the PR, 400 runs
claims.population: 180 UI build jobs: 117 compiled (median compile step 413 s), 32 reused a product
claims.note: Before-only figure from the PR body. About 75 compile-minutes an hour. This PR targets the first group (where the product is on a pool the run can use) plus the timing misses its wait catches; how many of the 917 minutes it removes is not measured yet.

records.title: Build cmuxTests without the compilation cache so it rebuilds incrementally
records.summary: Under the compilation cache, every cmuxTests build rewrote a chained bridging header that all 1,073 test inputs depend on, so a one-test-file edit recompiled the whole test target. The CI compile script now turns the cache off for cmuxTests only, and swift-driver's incremental build recompiles just the edited file. The app and every package keep the cache.
